extraction.Name: William Patton
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want the patent in fee to his 160 acre allotment, when it was issued, April 13, 1918, for he did not want to pay taxes; but the Indian Agency informed him that, if he did not take care of it, the land would be assessed for taxes, for which it would later be sold; so he accepted the patent in fee
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold his allotment to Harry Evans, of Pine Ridge, South Dakota, for $600.00 cash
extraction.Buyer: Harry Evans, of Pine Ridge, South Dakota, for $600.00 cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: paid the taxes out of this $600.00
extraction.Occupation/Income: mail carrier for the United States Government; runs a freight line from Rushville, Nebraska, to Oglala, South Dakota; raises a few hogs; these three enterprises constituting his entire income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, has good health; has a wife and seven children to support, all of whom have good health; considers he got a pretty poor price for his land; never sold his land for debts incurred before receiving the patent in fee; has never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; allotment was 160 acres; document No. 6801; sworn December 17, 1928, County of Shannon, State of South Dakota | TASK 5 BULK ALLOTMENT RECOVERY 2026-04-29: Sonnet text-extraction captured the allotment number from the source page header but classified it in NOTES as a 'document number' / 'Document No.' / 'No. NNNN' instead of placing it in the structured Allotment number field. The hypothesis that these document/file references are actually allotment numbers was confirmed via BLM cross-reference (exemplars: Eugene Means 2249, Lucy Patton 6802). This patch corrects 48 records via bulk regex extraction from NOTES with user-supervised review of every HIGH-confidence proposal. | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Oglala (Pine Ridge Agency)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')

recovery_notes.rationale: Source page header contained 'No. NNNN' which Sonnet captured in NOTES as 'document number' rather than placing in structured Allotment field. Hypothesis confirmed via BLM cross-reference.
Pine Ridge tribe field had 40+ string variants across the corpus. Consolidating to canonical 'Pine Ridge' for clean tabulation while preserving original variant in NOTES for audit.
